query: My doctor says my cholesterol is borderline high. Should I start statins or try to manage it with lifestyle changes first?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Mayo Clinic, Rochester MN USA): For patients with borderline cholesterol and low 10-year cardiovascular risk, lifestyle modification — diet, exercise, weight loss — is recommended for 3–6 months before considering statin therapy.

Source 2 (2022, NEJM, Boston MA USA): Statins reduce LDL cholesterol by 30–50% and significantly reduce cardiovascular events even in patients with modest baseline risk — the absolute benefit depends on baseline risk, not just cholesterol level.

Source 3 (2023, WebMD, Atlanta GA USA): Diet changes including reduced saturated fat, increased soluble fiber, and plant sterols can lower LDL by 10–20% — meaningful but often insufficient alone for patients with family history or multiple risk factors.

Source 4 (2022, Reddit r/AskDocs, USA): Community experience is mixed — many users found statin side effects (muscle aches, fatigue) intolerable; others report no side effects and credit statins with dramatically improved lipid profiles without lifestyle changes.

Source 5 (2021, JAMA Cardiology, Chicago IL USA): A 10-year cardiovascular risk calculator (PCE) should guide statin decisions — patients with borderline risk (5–7.5%) benefit from a risk discussion with their physician weighing statin benefits against side effect risk and patient preference.
plausible_answers: Try dietary changes and exercise for 3–6 months first, since lifestyle can meaningfully lower LDL without medication side effects.
Start statins now if you have family history, multiple risk factors, or 10-year cardiovascular risk above 7.5%.
Use a cardiovascular risk calculator with your physician first, since statin benefit depends on baseline risk, not cholesterol alone.
